- **BuildKit** (the only image started by this module):
  `docker.io/moby/buildkit:v0.34.1-rootless@sha256:f68752a5a94acfcdad2d07867b7075601a421638e17fc5f28efc1c814d0c4f89`
- **Daemon identity**: container `easy-host-buildkitd`, label `io.easy-host.role=buildkit`, socket `<root>/buildkit/socket/buildkitd.sock`.

### Exact runtime command (spike §3, no extra flags)
```
podman run -d --name easy-host-buildkitd \
  --label io.easy-host.role=buildkit \
  --user 0 --privileged \
  --entrypoint /usr/bin/buildkitd \
  -v <root>/buildkit/state:/home/user/.local/share/buildkit \
  -v <root>/buildkit/socket:/run/user/1000/buildkit \
  docker.io/moby/buildkit:v0.34.1-rootless@sha256:f68752a5a94acfcdad2d07867b7075601a421638e17fc5f28efc1c814d0c4f89 \
  --addr unix:///run/user/1000/buildkit/buildkitd.sock \
  --oci-worker-no-process-sandbox
```
`--privileged` is scoped to this infrastructure container only and is justified by the Phase 0 spike (`PRD-SP-03`). The daemon never receives app flags, host networking, or a shared app namespace.

### Behaviour delivered
- `Buildkit.ensure()` reuses a running managed container whose socket accepts a connection; otherwise it replaces/creates the container and waits a bounded 20 s for the socket.
- Cold-start timeout and start failures raise `PrerequisiteError` (exit 2); foreign container names and socket collisions raise `ConflictError` (exit 6); stale socket files are removed before a cold start; non-socket files on the socket path are refused.
- `status()` is read-only (never starts/stops) and returns `running | unhealthy | stopped | absent | conflict | unknown`; `stop()` is idempotent and never touches a foreign container.
- Every Podman call uses an argument array through the injectable `BuildkitRunner` seam with finite timeouts.

handoff.summary: Implemented the rootless buildkitd lifecycle in src/platform/buildkit.ts with ensure, status, and stop behind an injectable argument-array process runner; cold start uses the exact spike flags, reuses a healthy daemon, removes stale sockets, distinguishes name/socket conflicts, and enforces finite readiness and command timeouts. Added 21 unit tests using a recording fake runner and real temporary unix sockets; typecheck, lint, focused tests (21), full unit suite (333), and build all pass.
decisions: Container identity is easy-host-buildkitd with io.easy-host.role=buildkit; a container using that name without the label is foreign and is never removed, and a live socket without the managed container is a conflict rather than an adopted daemon.
Cold-start readiness is bounded at 20s with 100ms probes and a 1s probe timeout; podman run has a 600s budget for the cold image pull, inspect 15s, stop/rm 30s.

Lifecycle errors are PrerequisiteError exit 2 (socket timeout, start failure, podman missing, state unwritable) and ConflictError exit 6 (name/socket collision); BLD-1.3 remains responsible for mapping an unreachable daemon to build infrastructure-failure exit 3.
No --restart flag is added: the task requires flags to match the spike record exactly, and the spike command has no restart policy.
The shared platform runner does not exist yet, so buildkit.ts exposes a structurally compatible BuildkitRunner seam and ships a shell-free spawnSync default that can be replaced by injection.
interfaces: Buildkit.ensure(): Promise<BuildkitDaemon>; Buildkit.status(): Promise<BuildkitStatus>; Buildkit.stop(): Promise<BuildkitStopResult>
BuildkitDaemon { containerName, containerId, image, socketPath, buildkitHost, reused, state }
BuildkitStatus { state, socketReachable, detail, containerId, socketPath, buildkitHost }
BuildkitRunner { run(command, args, {timeoutMs}) } structurally compatible with the shared platform runner
tests: npm test -- tests/unit/buildkit.test.ts: 21 passed (3 consecutive runs)
warnings: The real privileged buildkitd was not started in this task; the spike-approved flags are reused verbatim and BLD-1.6 owns the gated real-host proof.

The feature document's open-question default mentions --restart=unless-stopped, but it is omitted because this task requires the exact spike flag set; the daemon persists while its container runs and cold-starts after stop or reboot.
Operations-guide documentation of --privileged and the exact flags is still owed by docs-engineer/DOC-1.4; the verified commands and justification are supplied above.
The aarch64 Railpack asset remains verified by digest only; no build lifecycle difference applies to buildkitd.
